text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today and has dropped 11% over the past two weeks, tracking a broader sell-off in oil stocks as crude prices have weakened—US oil is trading near $100 a barrel, down from levels earlier this month. The company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, and the decline accelerated sharply the next day, suggesting investors may have reacted negatively to the financial results or guidance relative to their expectations.

The midterm election results, which favored candidates less opposed to renewable energy expansion, add longer-term pressure on the oil sector. While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East persist (reflected in the gap between US and world oil prices), the political headwind against fossil fuels and soft crude pricing are working against energy stocks right now.
